accessNotes: visx is a low-level chart primitive library, not a style guide; airbnb.io/visx redirects to visx.airbnb.tech, a client-rendered Next.js app (no readable HTML). Defaults were read from the visx source on GitHub: the @visx/xychart lightTheme/darkTheme (the only opinionated theme), @visx/axis, @visx/grid and @visx/tooltip default props, and gallery demo sandboxes. Airbnb has no public data-visualisation style guide; Airbnb DLS brand values (Rausch #FF385C, Cereal font, #222222 text) come only from third-party design-system write-ups (superdesign.dev, designmd.co found via web search) and are NOT verified first-party.
summary: visx (Airbnb's React + D3 primitives library) is deliberately unopinionated, so its 'house look' is the XYChart light theme and the gallery demos: Open Color hues (dark cyan, light cyan, gold, coral, purples), gray #adb5bd gridlines, a heavy 2px near-black x-axis line, small bold-ish system-font labels. The gallery demos are playful and poster-like — full-bleed gradient backgrounds in rounded 14px cards with translucent white/teal marks and few or no axes. Airbnb's own product brand (Rausch red, Cereal) is not encoded in visx.

colors.categoricalNotes: XYChart lightTheme 'defaultColors' in order: cyan[9], cyan[3], yellow[5], red[4], grape[8], grape[5], pink[9] from the Open Color scale (colors.ts 'allColors'). Dark theme order: #3bc9db, #c3fae8, #ffec99, #ff8787, #e599f7, #be4bdb, #faa2c1. Seven colours only; no count-specific palettes.
colors.notes: No sequential/diverging scales are defined in visx; the 'sequential' entry above is the Open Color cyan ramp exported in xychart colors.ts (allColors.cyan, light→dark) and is only a convenient ramp, not a declared sequential palette. Light theme: background #fff, tick labels gray[7] #495057, axis labels gray[9] #212529, grid gray[5] #adb5bd, x-axis line gray[9] #212529. Dark theme: background #222, tick labels #e9ecef, axis labels #f8f9fa, grid #ced4da, x-axis line #f1f3f5. Raw primitive defaults (outside xychart): axis/ticks stroke #222, tick labels Arial 10px #222, GridRows/GridColumns stroke #eaf0f6. Gallery demo colours: barstack purples #6c5efb/#c998ff/#a44afe on #eaedff; bars demo rgba(23,233,217,.5) on GradientTealBlue. 'highlight' #ff385c is Airbnb's Rausch brand red per third-party DLS write-ups, not used by visx.

axisTitle.placement: x: centred below axis; y: rotated, offset dx -1.25em left of ticks

typography.notes: XYChart 'svgLabelBig' (axis titles, annotations): system stack, 700 weight, 12px, letter-spacing 0.4, text-anchor middle, #212529. 'svgLabelSmall' (tick labels): weight 200 (thin), 11px, #495057, letter-spacing 0.4. HTML labels (tooltips) inherit the 700/12px style. visx renders no chart titles; titles are left to the host app. Airbnb product font is Airbnb Cereal (third-party sources).

structure.gridlines: Optional Grid component; xychart theme grid stroke #adb5bd 1px solid; raw @visx/grid default #eaf0f6 1px. Demos typically show horizontal (rows) and/or vertical (columns) grids in light tints.
structure.axisLine: x-axis line heavy: 2px #212529 (gridColorDark); y-axis line light: 1px #adb5bd (gridColor).
structure.ticks: Yes, 4px tick marks in #adb5bd (light theme tickLength 4); raw @visx/axis default tickLength 8, stroke #222, square line-cap.
structure.frame: none in the theme; gallery demos wrap each chart in a full-bleed coloured/gradient rect with rx=14 rounded corners
structure.background: #ffffff (light) / #222 (dark); demos use gradients (e.g. GradientTealBlue) or tints like #eaedff
structure.notes: Tick labels end-anchored on the y axis (dx -0.25em).

legend.placement: Demo barstack: legend in a row above the chart, centred, 14px text
legend.notes: @visx/legend provides Ordinal/Linear/Threshold/Size legends; placement is left to the developer.

marks.bars: Demo bars: band padding 0.4, square corners, no outline, translucent fill rgba(23,233,217,.5) over gradient. Stacked bars demo: purple shades, no gaps.
marks.lines: Gallery 'Lines' tile: thin 1px white curved lines on #222 dark background; no points.
marks.areas: Gallery areas fill with vertical white-to-transparent gradient (LinearGradient) under a light stroke; stacked areas use warm pink→yellow gradients.
marks.points: Gallery dots: small solid gold circles on pink→coral gradient.
marks.notes: visx draws nothing by default; everything is composed explicitly.

labels.notes: Formatting left to d3-format/d3-time-format in user code.

furniture.title: Gallery tiles: bold white chart-type title centred near the bottom of each card with the component name in monospace below (e.g. 'Bars' / '<Shape.Bar />').
furniture.other: Rounded (rx 14) full-bleed card backgrounds are the signature of the demo gallery.

annotations: @visx/annotation provides Connector + CircleSubject + Label (title bold, subtitle normal) with optional background box; styles user-defined.
layout: Charts are responsive via ParentSize/withParentSize; demos use generous margins (bars demo verticalMargin 120).
interaction: Default tooltip (@visx/tooltip defaultStyles): white background, text #666666, padding 0.3rem 0.5rem, border-radius 3px, 14px, box-shadow 0 1px 2px rgba(33,33,33,0.2), line-height 1em. Barstack demo tooltip: rgba(0,0,0,0.9) black box with white text, series name bold in its series colour, small date line. XYChart supports crosshair glyphs and shared tooltips.
accessibility: @visx/pattern provides line/hatch/circle/wave/path patterns for texture fills (shown in the gallery 'Patterns' tile). XYChart demo honours prefers-reduced-motion.

chartTypes.notes: visx is primitive-based; all chart types are possible.

distinctiveRules.rule: Default categorical order is dark teal #0b7285, light cyan #66d9e8, gold #fcc419, coral #ff8787, purple #9c36b5, orchid #cc5de8, burgundy #a61e4d (Open Color steps).
distinctiveRules.quote: defaultColors = [cyan[9], cyan[3], yellow[5], red[4], grape[8], grape[5], pink[9]]

distinctiveRules.rule: x-axis domain line is heavy (2px, near-black #212529) while the y-axis line is thin (1px, #adb5bd grey).
distinctiveRules.quote: x.bottom.axisLine { stroke: gridColorDark, strokeWidth: 2 } … y.left.axisLine { stroke: gridColor, strokeWidth: 1 }

distinctiveRules.rule: Tick labels are 11px in a thin (200) weight with 0.4 letter-spacing; axis titles 12px bold (700).
distinctiveRules.quote: baseTickLabel { fontWeight: 200, fontSize: 11 }; defaultLabelStyles { fontWeight: 700, fontSize: 12, letterSpacing: 0.4 }

distinctiveRules.rule: Gridlines and tick marks share one grey #adb5bd at 1px; ticks are short (4px).
Dark theme uses #222 background with lighter tints of the same hues (#3bc9db, #c3fae8, #ffec99, #ff8787, #e599f7, #be4bdb, #faa2c1).
distinctiveRules.quote: backgroundColor: '#222', colors: [cyan[4], teal[1], yellow[2], red[4], grape[3], grape[6], pink[3]]

distinctiveRules.rule: Gallery demos render charts inside full-bleed gradient-filled cards with 14px rounded corners and translucent marks, often without axes.
Default tooltip is a small white card: #666 text, 14px, 3px radius, subtle 0 1px 2px shadow.
Raw primitive defaults (no theme): axis/tick stroke #222, tick labels Arial 10px #222, grid lines very pale #eaf0f6.
distinctiveRules.quote: defaultTextProps { fontFamily: 'Arial', fontSize: 10, fill: '#222' }; GridRows stroke = '#eaf0f6'

distinctiveRules.rule: Bar band padding 0.4 with square (non-rounded) bar ends in demos.

referenceImages.describes: 3×2 grid of rounded-corner gallery cards, each a full-bleed chart with no axes: 'Lines' – thin white wiggly lines on near-black #222; 'Bars' – translucent pale-cyan bars on a cyan→blue vertical gradient; 'Dots' – small gold dots on a pink→coral gradient; 'Patterns' – black line/hatch/dot/wave textures on cream; 'Areas' – a white-to-transparent gradient area chart on mint green with faint white grid; 'Stacked Areas' – wavy peach/yellow stacked areas on coral. Each card has a bold centred title near the bottom (e.g. 'Bars') with the monospace component name below ('<Shape.Bar />'), text coloured to match the card. No legends, sources or logos.

Minimal README example: ~26 thin vertical bars in solid bright red-orange on white, square ends, gaps roughly equal to bar width, no axes, gridlines, labels, title or legend — illustrating that visx draws only what you compose.
